title: Typed schema adapters
evidenceStatus: One recorded response decoded in four languages; 40 offline fixture executions and existing tests; frozen main 4c0c40d5; no provider calls
summary: All four adapters reproduce the recorded ticket and preserve its answers. A two-level score rubric loses its levels, TypeScript raw decoding accepts inherited option names, and absent confidence produces cross-language disagreement. The page needs executable semantic examples and a common conformance contract.
strengths: The page accurately discloses one shared response rather than four model runs.
Four recorded values and answer maps match; typed wrappers reject invalid options and numeric bounds.
Four TypeScript tests, five Rust tests, the Go suite and two Python contract tests passed.

findings.title: A two-level rubric loses its semantics
findings.evidence: TypeScript index.ts:81–100, Rust lib.rs:109–124, Go adapter.go:144–159 choose 0–1 noul before x-jev-levels. Probe confirms lost levels and TS acceptance of numeric/256 levels.
findings.impact: Explicit score semantics silently become a predicate/probability question, with language-specific supported shapes.
findings.fix: Prioritize explicit semantic metadata; validate rubric bounds/types and enum uniqueness against a shared schema profile.

findings.title: Raw decoding and acceptance policies diverge
findings.evidence: TypeScript index.ts:112 uses in; raw decode accepts constructor but final Zod parse rejects. Probe missing confidence is accepted in Python/Rust/Go, rejected in TS; optional distributions and choice/argmax disagreement are accepted by all.
findings.impact: A raw decoder violates its option contract and evidence completeness/coherence remain unspecified.
findings.fix: Use own-key/string checks and define missing/null, required evidence, coherence and extra-answer policies; preserve diagnostics and raw evidence.

findings.title: Visible examples omit mandatory descriptions
findings.evidence: misc.tsx:368–376 has no descriptions in all four snippets; TS probe fails with semantic description required: area. Actual repository demos include descriptions.
findings.impact: The central examples fail before transport and omit the information that makes a type semantic.
findings.fix: Generate UI snippets from executable, CI-compiled examples and display emitted questions.

findings.title: The live panel bypasses its adapter
findings.evidence: misc.tsx:377–439 manually maps answers and thresholds refund, keeps initial Python row when selecting another language and lacks input revision checks.
findings.impact: Validated value is presented without the advertised runtime adapter and stale responses can appear under changed text.
findings.fix: Run the TS compile/decode/Zod path, label actual execution language and bind evidence to input/schema revisions.

findings.title: One happy-path ticket is insufficient conformance evidence
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/adapters.py:22–69 records one three-field input, discards child emitted questions and records child errors without a run-level assertion.
findings.impact: Question parity, reference/rubric behavior and failure semantics cannot be established from shared values alone.
findings.fix: Publish a common versioned conformance corpus and require exact compiler/decoder agreement for supported features.

simulation.title: A contract workbench
simulation.description: Edit a fictional ticket field description or rubric, inspect emitted questions, replay recorded/manual/live answers through decoders, adjust review thresholds and undo complete revisions.
simulation.jevsRole: Judge support-request meaning under explicit field semantics; never issue a refund.
simulation.codeRole: Compile and validate schemas, preserve raw evidence, apply thresholds/review rules, own revisions and reject stale responses.
acceptanceCriteria: Visible snippets execute and supported questions match across languages.
Each result identifies input/schema revision and recorded/manual/live origin.
Invalid fixtures fail at the declared stage; no malformed answer becomes a valid ticket.
Changing thresholds preserves raw scores and undo restores the full checkpoint.
Keyboard users can inspect schema and evidence differences.

evaluation.design: 120 fixed conformance cases plus 1000 generated cases for each of five seeds produce 5120 cases/20480 four-language executions without provider calls. Optional 60-message semantic study, three repeats, yields 180 evaluations/540 decisions reused by all languages; 18 ten-message requests or 180 unbatched before retries. Independently label 30 counterfactual pairs, separate development data and report pair-clustered intervals.
baselines: Canonical compiler specification and direct language validators
Majority and keyword rules for the separate semantic study
metrics: Exact emitted-question parity and typed/evidence equality
Per-field/whole-ticket accuracy and error versus accepted coverage
Provider failure/retry counts and input/schema provenance

coverage.current: One recorded model input with three decisions, four decoders; audit adds ten fixtures × four decoder executions, not model judgments.
coverage.full: No external benchmark. Proposed declared 120 fixed and 5000 generated conformance cases, plus a separate 60-message semantic study.
coverage.feasibility: Conformance is offline and all toolchains already exist locally. A semantic study needs an explicit request plan; none was run.
